Louis XVI of France was married to Marie.why: One of the best-known royal marriages; the pair is named together over ten thousand times verbatim.

sources.quote: She served from 1774 to 1792, as the wife of King Louis XVI.

Elizabeth I of England never married..why: Her lifelong single state is one of the best-known facts about her, the source of her name 'the Virgin Queen'.

sources.quote: Although she received many offers, she never married and remained childless; the reasons for this are not clear.

The wife of the French king guillotined.why: People say that Louis XVI was guillotined in 1793 and that Marie Antoinette was his wife, each all the time. Nobody names her as 'the wife of the king guillotined in 1793': that description of her is never used, though it is true.

Louis XVI's wife was born into the House.why: People say that Marie Antoinette was a Habsburg and that she was Louis XVI's wife. Nobody states the dynasty of 'Louis XVI's wife' as such, though it is true.

sources.query: Louis XVI's wife was a Habsburg

The mother of Louis XVI's wife was Maria.why: People say that Marie Antoinette's mother was Maria Theresa, and that Louis XVI's wife was Marie Antoinette. Nobody calls Maria Theresa 'the mother of Louis XVI's wife' (the mother-in-law form is nearly absent), though it is true.

sources.quote: On 19 April 1770, at the age of fifteen, Louis XVI married the fourteen-year-old Archduchess Maria Antonia of Austria, his second cousin once removed and the youngest daughter of Holy Roman Emperor Francis I and Empress Maria Theresa.
sources.note: The one place the composed link appears: through the marriage sentence, not as a statement about his wife's mother.

Louis XVI was the French king guillotine.why: The execution of Louis XVI in January 1793 is one of the best-known events of the Revolution.

sources.quote: On 21 January 1793, Louis XVI, at age 38, was beheaded by a guillotine on the Place de la Révolution.

sources.quote: Elizabeth was the only surviving child of Henry VIII and his second wife, Anne Boleyn.

Louis XVI was King of France..why: Louis XVI was King of France from 1774 to 1792.

Louis XVI was King of Spain..why: Deliberately false side fact: Louis XVI was King of France, not Spain.

sources.quote: Louis XVI (Louis-Auguste; French: [lwi sɛːz]; 23 August 1754 – 21 January 1793) was the last king of France before the fall of the monarchy during the French Revolution.

Louis XVI's wife died in 1793..why: Marie Antoinette's execution in 1793, months after her husband's, is a standard fact of the Revolution.

notes: Dev ABox revision whose edited relation carries symmetry: spouse_of is symmetric, so the edit reaches Elizabeth I's side of the marriage. The new spouse is Elizabeth I of England, who never married, rather than someone with a stored husband: with Queen Victoria (the earlier draft) 'Who was Victoria's husband?' could stay Prince Albert, since spouse_of is only 'one spouse at a time' and Albert is stored by name, so the answer was not determinate. Related near asks Elizabeth I's husband (symmetry): before 'no one: she never married', stored everywhere (the Virgin Queen); after, Louis XVI; no stored spouse competes. Related far follows the edit to the new wife and asks her country (composition with a stored original: Louis XVI's article introduces 'Austrian Archduchess Marie Antoinette'). The derived queries are worked out: a binding through a description of Louis XVI (the king guillotined in January 1793), and two compositions through "Louis XVI's wife" (her royal house, her mother), whose composed forms have no hits in Dolma while each premise is common. The edit is anachronistic (Elizabeth I died in 1603, Louis XVI was born in 1754); revision edits need not be plausible (README, Belief revision operation). Residual risks: related far rests on the wife's origin, as the derived house question does on her dynasty; a model may hedge on Elizabeth I's suitors (Robert Dudley), which the near question's audit shows before editing. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) except those marked approximate. Audit fix 2026-11-12: 'Which country was Louis XVI's wife from?' was answered 'France' by 3 of 4 models (the wife of a French king reads as from France), so the related-far question and the Austria bridge now ask where she was BORN (Austria; Marie Antoinette was born in Vienna). The mother check now reads 'Which of Henry VIII's wives was the mother of Queen Elizabeth I?' (Qwen3 and Olmo answered Margaret/Mary Tudor to the bare question). Audit fix 2026-11-13 (second round): 'In which country was Louis XVI's wife born?' was still answered France by 3 of 4 models, so related far now asks the year his wife died (1793; with the edit, Elizabeth I's 1603) via a bridge on the wife's death year.
